definitionEn: a large area of ground where dead people are buried
situation: Visiting the graves of relatives, or walking among old gravestones in a quiet, green place.

examples.text: Every November we visit my grandparents' graves in the village [[cemetery]].
Tourists come to the city's famous [[cemetery]] to see the graves of writers and composers.
The council plans to open a new [[cemetery]], as there is no room left for graves in the old one.

texts: The funeral procession slowly entered the [[cemetery]].
She likes to jog through the old [[cemetery]] because it's so quiet.
Several famous poets are buried in this [[cemetery]].

badCollocation.noteRu: По-русски «на кладбище», а по-английски — in the cemetery (похоронен там) или at the cemetery (был там).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Ворота кладбища — the cemetery gates. Grave — могила, tomb — склеп, funeral — похороны; ворот у них нет.

nuance.text: We walked around the old [[cemetery]] looking for our great-grandfather's name on the stones.
nuance.explanationRu: Cemetery — кладбище, территория с множеством могил. Grave — одна могила; ходить по ней, разыскивая имя прадеда среди камней, нельзя.

reverse.text: She put fresh flowers on her mother's [[grave]].
reverse.explanationRu: Цветы кладут на могилу — grave. Cemetery — всё кладбище, у одного человека его нет.

fixIt.text: Thousands of soldiers are buried in the war [[memorial]] just outside the town.
fixIt.explanationRu: War memorial — памятник погибшим, в нём не хоронят. Военное кладбище — war cemetery.

definitionEn: one of the two groups of politicians that together make up a parliament
senseNote: Выбрано значение «палата парламента» (the upper/lower chamber); значения «камера» и «зал» не рассматриваем.
situation: A new law has to be approved by both parts of parliament, the upper one and the lower one.

examples.text: The bill passed the lower [[chamber]] easily but is expected to face opposition in the Senate.
In a parliament with two [[chambers]], the upper one usually reviews laws passed by the lower one.
Our guide explained that members of the upper [[chamber]] are appointed, not elected.

texts: The law must be approved by the upper [[chamber]] before it takes effect.
The ruling party has a majority in the lower [[chamber]].
Some reformers want to abolish the second [[chamber]] altogether.

badCollocation.noteRu: Больничная палата — ward. Chamber — палата парламента или камера, но не комната в больнице.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Верхняя палата парламента — the upper chamber (или house). Ward — больничная палата, cabinet — правительство, camera — фотоаппарат.

nuance.text: The new law was approved by the lower [[chamber]] on Tuesday.
nuance.explanationRu: Chamber — палата парламента, где депутаты голосуют за законы. Cabinet — кабинет министров, «нижнего» кабинета не бывает.

reverse.text: The prime minister appointed two new ministers to her [[cabinet]].
reverse.explanationRu: Министров назначают в cabinet — кабинет министров. Chamber — палата парламента, туда министров не назначают.

fixIt.text: After passing the lower house, the bill now goes to the upper [[ward]] for a final vote.
fixIt.explanationRu: Ward — больничная палата. Палата парламента — chamber (или house).

rewrite.original: Both parts of parliament must approve the law.
rewrite.frame: The law must be approved by both ____ of parliament.

definitionEn: a state of complete confusion and disorder
senseNote: Основное значение «хаос, неразбериха»; уровень C1 — в сочетаниях descend into chaos, throw into chaos, cause chaos.
situation: Nobody knows what is happening: trains are cancelled, people are shouting and nothing works properly.

examples.text: Heavy snow caused [[chaos]] on the roads, with thousands of drivers stuck overnight.
Without a clear leader, the meeting quickly descended into [[chaos]].
With three kids and a new puppy, our kitchen is total [[chaos]] every morning.

texts: The strike threw the city's transport system into [[chaos]].
After the flood, the town was in complete [[chaos]].
The new software caused [[chaos]] in the accounts department.

badCollocation.noteRu: Chaos — неисчисляемое, артикль a не нужен: It was total chaos. Про беспорядок в комнате говорят a mess.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Скатиться в хаос — descend into chaos. Havoc употребляют с cause или wreak, mess — с артиклем (a mess), а chaotic — прилагательное.

nuance.text: The rail strike threw the whole country into [[chaos]].
nuance.explanationRu: Chaos — масштабная неразбериха: страна, транспорт, экономика. Mess — беспорядок в комнате или «бардак» в делах, и с ним нужен артикль: a mess.

reverse.text: You've spilled coffee all over the table — what a [[mess]]!
reverse.explanationRu: Пролитый кофе — это a mess. Chaos неисчисляемое и слишком масштабное: what a chaos сказать нельзя.

fixIt.text: There was complete [[chaotic]] at the station after all the trains were cancelled.
fixIt.explanationRu: После complete нужно существительное: complete chaos. Chaotic — прилагательное «хаотичный».

wordFormation.text: The first week at the new office was [[chaotic]], but things soon settled down.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How was your first day back after the holidays?"
options: Total chaos! Everything went perfectly smoothly.
Total chaos! Three people were off sick and the printer broke.
It was a chaos, honestly, a real chaos.
reply.explanationRu: Total chaos — «полный хаос», и второй ответ объясняет почему. Первый противоречит сам себе, в третьем ошибка: chaos употребляется без артикля a.

rewrite.original: The storm caused complete disorder at the airport.

definitionEn: the way a writer or actor makes the people in a story seem real
senseNote: Выбрано значение из литературы и кино — «проработка персонажей»; значение «описание, характеристика» не рассматриваем.
situation: A critic discusses how believable and complex the people in a novel, play or series feel.

examples.text: The plot is predictable, but the [[characterization]] is subtle and convincing.
I love the show's [[characterization]]: even the villains feel like real, complicated people.
The actress spent months studying real nurses to perfect her [[characterization]].

texts: Strong [[characterization]] is what makes this novel unforgettable.
The film's weak [[characterization]] left the audience bored.
Her [[characterization]] of the grumpy detective won her an award.

badCollocation.noteRu: Характеристика с места работы — a reference. Characterization — проработка персонажей в книге или фильме.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Проработка персонажей — characterization. Characteristic — характерная черта, characterize — глагол, characteristically — наречие.

nuance.text: The [[characterization]] is weak: none of the people in the book feel real.
nuance.explanationRu: Characterization — то, как автор создаёт живых, убедительных персонажей. Plot — сюжет, цепочка событий; к тому, что люди в книге не кажутся живыми, он не относится.

reverse.text: The [[plot]] is full of twists, so you never know what will happen next.
reverse.explanationRu: Неожиданные повороты — это plot, сюжет. Characterization отвечает за персонажей, а не за события.

fixIt.text: Critics praised the author's [[characteristic]] of the lonely old fisherman.
fixIt.explanationRu: Characteristic — характерная черта. То, как автор изображает героя, — characterization.

wordFormation.text: The novel is praised for its rich [[characterization]] and vivid dialogue.

definitionEn: to be a typical feature or quality of something
senseNote: Выбрано значение «быть характерной чертой» (be characterized by); значение «описывать как» (characterize as) не рассматриваем.
situation: Describing the typical features of a period, a region or a style in an essay or report.

examples.text: The region is [[characterized]] by long, cold winters and short summers.
The 1960s were [[characterized]] by rapid social change and new styles of music.
Sudden mood swings and poor sleep [[characterize]] this rare condition in teenagers.

texts: Her early paintings are [[characterized]] by bright, bold colours.
The talks were [[characterized]] by mutual distrust.
The city's economy is [[characterized]] by small family businesses.

badCollocation.noteRu: После characterized нужен предлог by: characterized by cold winters. With здесь ошибка.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Отличаться, характеризоваться» — be characterized by. Featured и described так не употребляются, а typical требует of: typical of.

nuance.text: The region is [[characterized]] by dry summers and mild, rainy winters.
nuance.explanationRu: Be characterized by — «характеризоваться, отличаться». Feature в пассиве с by в таком смысле не используют: можно сказать the region features dry summers.

reverse.text: The film [[features]] a beautiful soundtrack by a young composer.
reverse.explanationRu: Feature — «включать, показывать»: в фильме звучит саундтрек. Characterize — «быть типичной чертой», фильм не может «характеризовать саундтрек».

fixIt.text: In many countries, the 1990s were [[described]] by economic crisis and rapid change.
fixIt.explanationRu: Described by значит «описаны кем-то». Отличаться, характеризоваться чем-то — be characterized by.

wordFormation.text: Heavy rain and strong winds [[characterize]] the local climate in autumn.

rewrite.original: Long, cold winters are typical of the region.
rewrite.frame: The region is ____ long, cold winters.

definitionEn: the quality of being pleasant and attractive, especially of a place or thing
senseNote: Выбрано значение «очарование, прелесть (места, вещи)»; обаяние человека — более базовое, «амулет» — другое значение.
situation: Describing why an old village, a small café or an old house feels so pleasant and special.

examples.text: The old town has kept its [[charm]] despite the crowds of tourists.
The cottage is small and a bit cold, but that's part of its [[charm]].
Much of the film's [[charm]] comes from its gentle humour and old-fashioned music.

texts: The village has lost much of its [[charm]] since the motorway was built.
I love the old-world [[charm]] of this little hotel.
Handwritten letters have a [[charm]] that emails will never have.

badCollocation.noteRu: Перед существительным нужно прилагательное: a charming town. Charm — существительное: the town's charm.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Очарование старины — old-world charm, устойчивое сочетание. Attraction, sweetness и delight с old-world не употребляются.

nuance.text: The old harbour has a [[charm]] that new buildings can never copy.
nuance.explanationRu: Charm — очарование, оно бывает у места, вещи или человека. Charisma — харизма, особая сила личности; у гавани или здания её не бывает.

fixIt.text: The tiny café has a special [[glamour]]: mismatched chairs, old books and the smell of fresh bread.
fixIt.explanationRu: Glamour — роскошь и блеск, а разномастные стулья и старые книги — это уютное очарование, charm.

wordFormation.text: We stayed in a [[charming]] little guest house by the lake.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Is your village worth visiting, or is it just boring?"
options: Honestly, it has no charm at all, so you'll love it!
It possesses, one might argue, a certain rustic charm.
It's quiet, but that's part of its charm. Come and see!
reply.explanationRu: Part of its charm — «в этом и есть его прелесть», третий ответ естественный. Первый нелогичен, второй звучит книжно и напыщенно для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: a formal document that sets out the rights, aims or principles of an organization
senseNote: Выбрано значение «устав, хартия»; значение «чартер, аренда самолёта» не рассматриваем.
situation: An international organization writes down its basic aims and the rights of its members.

examples.text: Under its [[charter]], the organization must protect the rights of all member states.
The company has signed a [[charter]] promising equal pay for men and women.
The university received its royal [[charter]] in the fifteenth century.

texts: The city's first [[charter]] was granted in 1215.
All members must respect the club's [[charter]].
The new [[charter]] guarantees patients' right to see their records.

badCollocation.noteRu: Подписать хартию — sign the charter, без under. Under the charter значит «согласно уставу».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Хартия прав — a charter of rights. Chart — диаграмма, character — характер или персонаж, chapter — глава книги.

nuance.text: The organization's [[charter]] sets out its aims and the rights of its members.
nuance.explanationRu: Charter — устав или хартия, где записаны цели организации и права её членов. Contract — договор между сторонами; цели организации в нём не формулируют.

reverse.text: Before starting the job, read your employment [[contract]] carefully.
reverse.explanationRu: Трудовой договор — employment contract. Charter — устав организации, а не соглашение с работником.

fixIt.text: The UN [[Statute]] was signed in San Francisco in 1945.
fixIt.explanationRu: Устав ООН — the UN Charter. Statute — закон, принятый парламентом.

definitionEn: lasting for a long time and difficult to cure or solve
senseNote: О болезнях и о проблемах: chronic pain, a chronic shortage of teachers.
situation: A doctor talks about an illness that never really goes away, or a problem that lasts for years.

examples.text: She has suffered from [[chronic]] back pain since a car accident ten years ago.
Rural schools face a [[chronic]] shortage of qualified maths teachers.
Doctors warn that [[chronic]] lack of sleep can damage your health.

texts: Asthma is a [[chronic]] condition that needs regular treatment.
The city has a [[chronic]] housing problem.
The club's [[chronic]] lack of money finally forced it to close.

badCollocation.noteRu: Chronic — длящийся месяцами и годами. Про сильную вчерашнюю головную боль говорят a bad или a terrible headache.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Хроническая нехватка — a chronic shortage. Chronical — ошибка, chronological — «хронологический», а long shortage так не говорят.

nuance.text: Arthritis is a [[chronic]] disease: most patients live with it for decades.
nuance.explanationRu: Chronic — хроническая болезнь, длится годами. Acute — острая: начинается внезапно и протекает бурно, десятилетиями острой болезнь не бывает.

reverse.text: He was rushed to hospital with [[acute]] appendicitis.
reverse.explanationRu: Острый аппендицит — acute appendicitis: он внезапный и требует срочной помощи. Chronic означало бы болезнь, которая тянется годами.

fixIt.text: My grandmother has a [[chronical]] heart condition and takes pills every day.
fixIt.explanationRu: Прилагательное — chronic, без -al: a chronic heart condition. Chronical — типичная ошибка по аналогии с русским «хронический».

wordFormation.text: Many hospitals are [[chronically]] short of nurses.

reply.context: A colleague says: "You look exhausted. Is everything OK?"
options: Not really. I've got chronic insomnia — I haven't slept properly for months.
Not really. I've had chronic insomnia since last night.
I am afflicted by a chronic sleep disorder of considerable severity.
reply.explanationRu: Chronic insomnia — бессонница, которая длится месяцами, первый ответ логичен. «Хроническая со вчерашнего вечера» — противоречие, третий ответ звучит как медицинская справка.

definitionEn: a fairly large part or amount of something
senseNote: Выбрано значение «значительная часть» (a big chunk of my salary), а не «кусок сыра или хлеба».
situation: Complaining that rent, travel or one task takes up a big part of your money or time.

examples.text: Rent now eats up a huge [[chunk]] of my monthly salary.
I spent a big [[chunk]] of the weekend answering work emails.
Online sales now account for a large [[chunk]] of the company's profits.

texts: Commuting takes a big [[chunk]] out of my day.
A large [[chunk]] of the budget goes on marketing.
We've already finished a good [[chunk]] of the work.

badCollocation.noteRu: Совет — a piece of advice (или some advice). Chunk — «большая часть» денег, времени, работы, а не отдельный совет.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Значительная часть зарплаты — a big chunk of my salary. Lump и block — «глыба, брусок», crumb — «крошка»; о доле денег так не говорят.

nuance.text: Taxes swallow a huge [[chunk]] of what I earn.
nuance.explanationRu: Chunk — большая часть чего-то (дохода, времени). Bit — «немного, кусочек», и с huge это противоречит.

reverse.text: Could I have a [[bit]] of milk in my tea, please?
reverse.explanationRu: Немного молока — a bit of milk. Chunk — большой кусок или большая доля, к жидкости не подходит.

fixIt.text: Preparing for the exam took a huge [[piece]] of my free time.
fixIt.explanationRu: О большой части времени или денег говорят a huge chunk. A piece of my free time звучит неестественно.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How's the new flat? Is it expensive?"
options: I love it, and there's a huge chunk of cheese in every room.
I love it, but the rent takes a huge chunk of my salary.
The rental expenditure constitutes a significant chunk of my remuneration.
reply.explanationRu: A huge chunk of my salary — «большая часть зарплаты», второй ответ естественный. Первый понимает chunk буквально, третий смешивает канцелярит с разговорным chunk.

rewrite.original: A large part of the money was spent on advertising.
rewrite.frame: A ____ of the money was spent on advertising.

definitionEn: to produce large amounts of something quickly, often without much care
senseNote: Выбрано значение churn out — «штамповать, клепать»; прямые значения «сбивать масло» и «бурлить» не рассматриваем.
situation: A factory, writer or studio produces huge numbers of similar things very quickly, caring more about quantity than quality.

examples.text: The studio [[churns]] out three or four cheap comedies every year.
She [[churned]] out a new crime novel every six months to pay the bills.
The factory can [[churn]] out ten thousand phone cases a day.

texts: Some influencers [[churn]] out videos every single day.
Fast-fashion brands [[churn]] out cheap clothes that fall apart.
Politicians often [[churn]] out the same tired slogans.

badCollocation.noteRu: Churn out — выпускать много и быстро, часто без особого качества. Про один шедевр говорят create или produce a masterpiece.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Штамповать дешёвые романы — churn out cheap novels. Spit out, shake out и whip out значат «выплюнуть», «вытряхнуть» и «быстро достать».

nuance.text: The factory [[churns]] out thousands of cheap plastic toys every day.
nuance.explanationRu: Churn out — штамповать, выпускать массово. Carry out — «выполнять, проводить» (исследование, задачу); игрушки так не «проводят».

reverse.text: Police [[carried]] out a search of the building.
reverse.explanationRu: Провести обыск — carry out a search. Churn out — штамповать продукцию, обыск нельзя «наштамповать».

fixIt.text: The studio [[stamps]] out a new superhero film every few months.
fixIt.explanationRu: Stamp out — «искоренить, покончить с чем-то», ложный друг русского «штамповать». Штамповать фильмы — churn out.

rewrite.original: The company quickly produces hundreds of cheap, similar apps every year.
rewrite.frame: The company ____ hundreds of cheap apps every year.
rewrite.explanationRu: Штамповать в больших количествах — churn out.
